source: Bush, R. 2008. 'Nutrition', ACIAR AH 2005/086 workshop slides, University of Sydney (mekonglivestock.wordpress.com)
text: This nutrition guidance ties feed quantity and quality to the animal's current production demand: maintenance needs the least (around 4kg dry matter/day fresh-forage equivalent), draught work more (around 6kg DM/day), pregnancy and/or lactation more again (8-10kg DM/day), and fattening the most (10-12kg DM/day). Forage quality is described in three grades: high quality is young, green, actively-growing plant material that hasn't yet flowered, with many leaves relative to stem; medium quality is more mature, a green-and-dead mix in mid-to-late flowering with some seed head present, and a lower leaf-to-stem ratio; low quality is old, dry leaf and stem, hard and woody, with or without seed head. For breeding cows and young calves, supplements such as rice straw, grasses and hay, fodder trees, and green or dried maize are recommended, alongside routine mineral supplementation (especially salt). Calves need colostrum within the first hours after birth, and nursing cows need ample feed and water to produce sufficient milk.
